tools.name: list_repo
tools.description: List every file in the repository under repair (paths relative to the repo root). Call once before exploring.
args: cd "${REPAIR_WORKDIR:?REPAIR_WORKDIR not set}" && find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | sed 's|^\./||' | sort

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read one file from the repository under repair. Pass the repo-relative path exactly as listed by list_repo.
args: case "$1" in *..*|/*) echo "path rejected: $1" >&2; exit 1;; esac; cat "${REPAIR_WORKDIR:?REPAIR_WORKDIR not set}/$1"

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write the full new content of one file in the repository under repair. Pass the repo-relative path and the COMPLETE file content (this replaces the file).
args: case "$1" in *..*|/*) echo "path rejected: $1" >&2; exit 1;; esac; d="${REPAIR_WORKDIR:?REPAIR_WORKDIR not set}/$1"; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$d")"; printf '%s' "$2" > "$d" && echo "wrote $1 ($(wc -c < "$d") bytes)"

tools.name: scan_repo
tools.description: Run the skeptic security scanner over the repository under repair and return its findings. Use it to check whether the defect class is still present after your edits.
args: "${SKEPTIC_BIN:?SKEPTIC_BIN not set}" scan --format text --mode ir "${REPAIR_WORKDIR:?REPAIR_WORKDIR not set}" 2>/dev/null || true

tools.name: run_repo_tests
tools.description: Run the repository's own test suite (make test) in the repository under repair and return the tail of its output.
args: cd "${REPAIR_WORKDIR:?REPAIR_WORKDIR not set}" && { make test 2>&1 || true; } | tail -c 4000

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Make one exact text replacement in one file of the repository under repair. Pass the repo-relative path, the exact text to find (must occur exactly once), and its replacement. Cheaper and safer than rewriting the whole file.
args:
case "$1" in *..*|/*) echo "path rejected: $1" >&2; exit 1;; esac
f="${REPAIR_WORKDIR:?REPAIR_WORKDIR not set}/$1"
[ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no such file: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
python3 - "$f" "$2" "$3" <<'PYEOF'
import sys
path, find, repl = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
text = open(path).read()
n = text.count(find)
if n == 0:
    print(f"find-text not present in {path}", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
if n > 1:
    print(f"find-text occurs {n} times in {path}; make it unique", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
open(path, "w").write(text.replace(find, repl, 1))
print(f"edited {path}: 1 replacement")
PYEOF
